analysis:
This batch contains documentation only. The new changelog changelog.d/qwen-end-of-prompt-checkpoints.md (head lines 1-13) describes a change for dense Qwen3.5/3.8 requests served alone. Such a request now also ends a prefill range just below its prompt end: at least 64 tokens before it, on the 256-token grid, when that saves at least 1,024 tokens. That boundary yields one more complete SSD checkpoint per request. The inference.md row added at head line 1406 documents demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens in EngineV2Factory+DemandedCheckpoint.swift. Base lines 1-805 of inference.md were examined as context and are unchanged.

Relevant threat: T-041 (A-001, ADV-001, ADV-002). The change places checkpoints closer to the prompt end, which may add one more encrypted at-rest artifact per request. The documentation keeps the same complete store, so the at-rest exposure is unchanged in kind if that holds: the same HMAC names, cacheSalt scope, TTL and benefit floor. The 1,024-token floor resembles T-041's per-donation benefit floor. Keeping at least 64 tokens before the end means the final prompt suffix is still not checkpointed. The added checkpoint may sharpen the same-account TTFT oracle (SEC-035), but that risk is already accepted.

No security regression is evidenced. Integration should verify these points in the Swift source, which is not supplied here:
- EngineV2Factory+DemandedCheckpoint.swift and the CBv2 scheduler apply the demanded boundary only with the request's cacheSalt and the existing complete-store donation gates (adoption bound/benefit floor, disk/endurance guards, repeat hint).
- The boundary computation cannot be driven by a consumer to bypass the gating or cause unbounded writes.
- Checkpoint capture at a non-stripe boundary restores exactly, which is a correctness concern related to T-007/T-027.
